data.claim: Command gates, per-project pipelines, reviewers, rules and promotion already carry the generic workflow; twelve specific gaps (IaC kind, plan-bound apply approval, cloud sandbox lifecycle, policy records, module kind, schema check, finding ingest, supply-chain verification, drift jobs, CI-platform and forge adapters, deployment records, compliance evidence) are not planned.
data.falsifier: A queue search finds planned tasks that already cover a listed gap, or a project of this kind cannot run its gates as command gates today.
data.mechanism: QUESTION: can ddflow, with what exists and what is planned, manage projects whose product is infrastructure as code (Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, CDK, Ansible, Helm, Kustomize, Packer, Crossplane, Bicep, CloudFormation), DevOps and DevSecOps work, and the CI/CD pipelines of GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Gitea and Azure DevOps? WHAT ALREADY WORKS TODAY: the gate pipeline is per-project data and any command can be a command gate (terraform fmt/validate/test, tflint, checkov, conftest, actionlint run as gates today); rules, decisions, lessons, goals engine (planned P-goals), leases and worktrees isolate agents, cross-family reviewers (Kimi, DeepSeek) review diffs, the codeguide and context7 companions serve standards and docs, ddflow promote tracks environment branches and recorded deploy shas, forge adapters (infra/forge.py) drive GitHub through gh and GitLab through glab for PR state, a ci gate runs the project's CI command set locally (D-ci-parity). Unavailable tools are recorded unavailable, never passed. WHAT IS PLANNED AND HELPS: SC-catalogue/SC-data-more (stack probe with an IaC data wave, data only), TF-flows-system pipeline-validate and TF-cadence (per-commit, per-PR, nightly, post-deploy sets), TD-emulation/TD-pins/TD-lease (containers, version pins and image digests, leases for scarce equipment), SE-ask-core approvals with content digests, SE-waiver, AG-deps-guard (dependencies agents add), P-safeguards (cards, consult action for context7/codeguide), P-schedule.watch, B-gap-checks-publish (gate state as a forge check), CP-intake (webhook intake), P-org-config (corporate policy layers), P-goals (measurable goals). THE WEB (2026): the IaC test pyramid is static (fmt, validate, tflint, checkov/trivy/tfsec/kics) about 70 percent, module-level plan and terraform test with mocks about 25 percent, apply-in-sandbox (Terratest) and nightly end-to-end about 5 percent; policy as code is OPA/Conftest or Sentinel run on the JSON plan (terraform show -json), first in warn mode then enforcing after two clean sprints; plan and apply are separated and the approved plan is what is applied (Atlantis, Spacelift, env0, HCP Terraform), with state locking and scheduled drift detection (plan -detailed-exitcode); modules are versioned by semver where removed variables, renamed outputs and changed resource types are breaking, published by git tag to a registry, documented by terraform-docs; HashiCorp ships a Terraform MCP server (registry search, provider docs, workspaces) and the TerraFormer paper (2026-01) and field reports show models hallucinate resource types and attributes, which a provider-schema check catches deterministically; DevSecOps means OIDC short-lived cloud credentials instead of static keys, SLSA provenance, Sigstore/cosign signatures, SBOMs, SARIF findings, secret scanning, and gates fast enough that nobody routes around them; pipelines are code with their own linters (actionlint, GitLab CI Lint API, the Jenkins declarative linter, Azure Pipelines validation, Gitea/Forgejo Actions on act_runner) and local runners (act, gitlab-ci-local). GAPS: (1) no first-class IaC stack kind with per-tool gate roles, tool and provider version pins and lock-file checks; (2) no plan record bound to commit, variables and workspace, so no 'apply only the plan that was approved' gate and no production-apply guard for agents; (3) no cloud sandbox lifecycle (TTL, guaranteed teardown, cost cap, orphan sweep, OIDC credentials) beyond local containers; (4) no policy-as-code record kind with enforce ramp and waivers with expiry mapped to executable bundles; (5) no module record kind (build, consume, semver by contract diff, registry provenance, lock hashes); (6) no provider-schema hallucination check and no registered Terraform MCP companion; (7) no SARIF/plan-JSON finding ingest with triage; (8) no provenance, signature and SBOM verification gate for images and modules; (9) no scheduled drift detection filing work; (10) forge support is GitHub and GitLab only (no Gitea/Forgejo, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket) and there is no CI-platform adapter for detect, lint, local run, status and logs, nor pipeline generation from ddflow's own gates with drift check; (11) no deployment, environment and release record beyond branch promotion (artifact digest, rollback plan, freeze windows, change-ticket link, post-deploy gates); (12) no compliance evidence pack mapping controls to gates.

data.question: Can ddflow's current and planned features manage infrastructure-as-code, DevOps and DevSecOps projects and the CI/CD pipelines of GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Gitea and Azure DevOps, and what is missing?

data.claim: The planned constellation covers the version pair, change request and drift ideas, but eleven specifics for infrastructure siblings (roles, environment contract adapters, artifact handoff, sibling proposals, deploy-aware matrix, plan impact, coordinated release, contract test, three-way drift, lifecycle, on-prem) are not planned.
data.falsifier: A read of CN-roles, CN-manifest, CN-matrix and CN-libs shows they already model environments, deployments or infrastructure contracts.
data.mechanism: QUESTION: an application project and a sister project that holds the pipelines and infrastructure as code for it (cloud or on-prem): how do they coordinate so ddflow keeps both in sync? WHAT THE CONSTELLATION PLANS (P-constellation, D-constellation): a manifest of member projects with roles, spec records with format adapters (OpenAPI, protobuf, ASN.1, YANG, DBC, register maps), digest-pinned cross-project references, consumer edges and an impact query, change requests with a consumer state machine (pending, acknowledged, adopting, adopted, not_affected), baselines, a compatibility matrix with a can-i-release gate, a breaking-change gate classified by the adapter's checker, shared library registry (CN-libs) with a bump workflow that never edits another project's lockfile, a read-only sibling mirror, optional push nudge (CN-dispatch), a scheduled drift audit, topologies single repo, monorepo, polyrepo, submodule umbrella. THE WEB: a typical split is an app repo whose CI builds the image and a separate GitOps config repo that Argo CD or Flux watches (separate so the CD system does not trigger itself); promotion is a pull request that bumps an image tag or module version per environment (separate directories, branches, repos, or tag promotion); Flux image automation or Kargo promotion tasks do it automatically; versions follow semver with scope prefixes; the contract between the two is inputs and outputs of modules, Helm values and schema, manifests, environment variables, ports and health endpoints; a Pact-style can-i-deploy asks whether this version pair is verified together. WHAT FITS TODAY: infra and app can be two constellation members; CN-matrix and the can-i-release gate express version pairs; CN-cr carries change requests; ddflow promote and CN-libs bump workflows cover tags. GAPS: (1) no member roles for app, infra, gitops-config, module-library and pipeline-library, and no gitops-config topology; (2) no environment contract kind with adapters for Terraform variables and outputs, Helm values schema, Kubernetes manifests (kubeconform), config and environment-variable schemas, so what the app NEEDS from the infrastructure and what the infrastructure PROVIDES is not machine-checked; (3) no artifact handoff record (image digest, chart or module version, SBOM, provenance) that the infra project consumes by digest; (4) no way to open a proposal in the sibling repository through the forge with a change request attached; (5) the matrix is release-time, not deploy-aware: no rows per environment from deployment records and no can-i-deploy gate before an apply or promotion; (6) no plan-impact analysis: an infra plan diff that changes an output the app uses, or an app change that adds an environment variable, must raise a change request in the other project; (7) no coordinated release workflow (ordering, expand and contract, shared rollback, freeze windows); (8) no environment contract test against terraform output or rendered manifests; (9) no three-way drift audit (declared in the infra repo, deployed per deployment records and cloud reads, running version and health); (10) no lifecycle workflows for decommission, rename, secret rotation (references only) and deprecation notices; (11) no on-prem and air-gapped support (Ansible inventories, Packer images, offline registry and provider mirrors, hardware leases); (12) pipeline libraries (GitHub reusable workflows, GitLab includes, Jenkins shared libraries, Azure templates) are not versioned or pinned like code libraries.

N1="""QUESTION: can ddflow, with what exists and what is planned, manage projects whose product is infrastructure as code (Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, CDK, Ansible, Helm, Kustomize, Packer, Crossplane, Bicep, CloudFormation), DevOps and DevSecOps work, and the CI/CD pipelines of GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Gitea and Azure DevOps? WHAT ALREADY WORKS TODAY: the gate pipeline is per-project data and any command can be a command gate (terraform fmt/validate/test, tflint, checkov, conftest, actionlint run as gates today); rules, decisions, lessons, goals engine (planned P-goals), leases and worktrees isolate agents, cross-family reviewers (Kimi, DeepSeek) review diffs, the codeguide and context7 companions serve standards and docs, ddflow promote tracks environment branches and recorded deploy shas, forge adapters (infra/forge.py) drive GitHub through gh and GitLab through glab for PR state, a ci gate runs the project's CI command set locally (D-ci-parity). Unavailable tools are recorded unavailable, never passed. WHAT IS PLANNED AND HELPS: SC-catalogue/SC-data-more (stack probe with an IaC data wave, data only), TF-flows-system pipeline-validate and TF-cadence (per-commit, per-PR, nightly, post-deploy sets), TD-emulation/TD-pins/TD-lease (containers, version pins and image digests, leases for scarce equipment), SE-ask-core approvals with content digests, SE-waiver, AG-deps-guard (dependencies agents add), P-safeguards (cards, consult action for context7/codeguide), P-schedule.watch, B-gap-checks-publish (gate state as a forge check), CP-intake (webhook intake), P-org-config (corporate policy layers), P-goals (measurable goals). THE WEB (2026): the IaC test pyramid is static (fmt, validate, tflint, checkov/trivy/tfsec/kics) about 70 percent, module-level plan and terraform test with mocks about 25 percent, apply-in-sandbox (Terratest) and nightly end-to-end about 5 percent; policy as code is OPA/Conftest or Sentinel run on the JSON plan (terraform show -json), first in warn mode then enforcing after two clean sprints; plan and apply are separated and the approved plan is what is applied (Atlantis, Spacelift, env0, HCP Terraform), with state locking and scheduled drift detection (plan -detailed-exitcode); modules are versioned by semver where removed variables, renamed outputs and changed resource types are breaking, published by git tag to a registry, documented by terraform-docs; HashiCorp ships a Terraform MCP server (registry search, provider docs, workspaces) and the TerraFormer paper (2026-01) and field reports show models hallucinate resource types and attributes, which a provider-schema check catches deterministically; DevSecOps means OIDC short-lived cloud credentials instead of static keys, SLSA provenance, Sigstore/cosign signatures, SBOMs, SARIF findings, secret scanning, and gates fast enough that nobody routes around them; pipelines are code with their own linters (actionlint, GitLab CI Lint API, the Jenkins declarative linter, Azure Pipelines validation, Gitea/Forgejo Actions on act_runner) and local runners (act, gitlab-ci-local). GAPS: (1) no first-class IaC stack kind with per-tool gate roles, tool and provider version pins and lock-file checks; (2) no plan record bound to commit, variables and workspace, so no 'apply only the plan that was approved' gate and no production-apply guard for agents; (3) no cloud sandbox lifecycle (TTL, guaranteed teardown, cost cap, orphan sweep, OIDC credentials) beyond local containers; (4) no policy-as-code record kind with enforce ramp and waivers with expiry mapped to executable bundles; (5) no module record kind (build, consume, semver by contract diff, registry provenance, lock hashes); (6) no provider-schema hallucination check and no registered Terraform MCP companion; (7) no SARIF/plan-JSON finding ingest with triage; (8) no provenance, signature and SBOM verification gate for images and modules; (9) no scheduled drift detection filing work; (10) forge support is GitHub and GitLab only (no Gitea/Forgejo, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket) and there is no CI-platform adapter for detect, lint, local run, status and logs, nor pipeline generation from ddflow's own gates with drift check; (11) no deployment, environment and release record beyond branch promotion (artifact digest, rollback plan, freeze windows, change-ticket link, post-deploy gates); (12) no compliance evidence pack mapping controls to gates."""
run(["research","add","--new","--id","R-iac-devops","--question","Can ddflow's current and planned features manage infrastructure-as-code, DevOps and DevSecOps projects and the CI/CD pipelines of GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Gitea and Azure DevOps, and what is missing?","--claim","Command gates, per-project pipelines, reviewers, rules and promotion already carry the generic workflow; twelve specific gaps (IaC kind, plan-bound apply approval, cloud sandbox lifecycle, policy records, module kind, schema check, finding ingest, supply-chain verification, drift jobs, CI-platform and forge adapters, deployment records, compliance evidence) are not planned.","--mechanism",N1,"--falsifier","A queue search finds planned tasks that already cover a listed gap, or a project of this kind cannot run its gates as command gates today.","--probe","queue grep for terraform, iac, pipeline, deploy, policy, drift, sandbox, gitea, azure, jenkins, sarif, sbom, slsa; read TF-flows-system, SC-data-more, TD-emulation, B-gap-checks-publish, CN-matrix, infra/forge.py; ddflow promote --help; ddflow companions","--probe-output","terraform/opentofu/pulumi/ansible/helm: 0 tasks; iac: SC-data-more (data only); gitea/azure devops/jenkins/bitbucket: 0; forge adapters: GitHub and GitLab only; promote: add/deployed/status by branch; sarif/slsa/sbom/cosign: 0 (AG-deps-guard covers app dependencies only)","--verdict","CONFIRMED","--sources","https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-02-23-how-to-implement-infrastructure-as-code-testing-pyramid-with-terraform/view; https://kokil.com.np/blog/policy-as-code-with-opa-and-conftest; https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/06/10/codex-cli-terraform-infrastructure-as-code-mcp-server-terrashark-pulumi-agent-skills/; https://www.env0.com/frameworks/atlantis-for-terraform-how-it-works-limitations-better-alternatives; https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-01-30-terraform-module-versioning/view; https://cloudaware.com/blog/zero-trust-devsecops/"])
N2="""QUESTION: an application project and a sister project that holds the pipelines and infrastructure as code for it (cloud or on-prem): how do they coordinate so ddflow keeps both in sync? WHAT THE CONSTELLATION PLANS (P-constellation, D-constellation): a manifest of member projects with roles, spec records with format adapters (OpenAPI, protobuf, ASN.1, YANG, DBC, register maps), digest-pinned cross-project references, consumer edges and an impact query, change requests with a consumer state machine (pending, acknowledged, adopting, adopted, not_affected), baselines, a compatibility matrix with a can-i-release gate, a breaking-change gate classified by the adapter's checker, shared library registry (CN-libs) with a bump workflow that never edits another project's lockfile, a read-only sibling mirror, optional push nudge (CN-dispatch), a scheduled drift audit, topologies single repo, monorepo, polyrepo, submodule umbrella. THE WEB: a typical split is an app repo whose CI builds the image and a separate GitOps config repo that Argo CD or Flux watches (separate so the CD system does not trigger itself); promotion is a pull request that bumps an image tag or module version per environment (separate directories, branches, repos, or tag promotion); Flux image automation or Kargo promotion tasks do it automatically; versions follow semver with scope prefixes; the contract between the two is inputs and outputs of modules, Helm values and schema, manifests, environment variables, ports and health endpoints; a Pact-style can-i-deploy asks whether this version pair is verified together. WHAT FITS TODAY: infra and app can be two constellation members; CN-matrix and the can-i-release gate express version pairs; CN-cr carries change requests; ddflow promote and CN-libs bump workflows cover tags. GAPS: (1) no member roles for app, infra, gitops-config, module-library and pipeline-library, and no gitops-config topology; (2) no environment contract kind with adapters for Terraform variables and outputs, Helm values schema, Kubernetes manifests (kubeconform), config and environment-variable schemas, so what the app NEEDS from the infrastructure and what the infrastructure PROVIDES is not machine-checked; (3) no artifact handoff record (image digest, chart or module version, SBOM, provenance) that the infra project consumes by digest; (4) no way to open a proposal in the sibling repository through the forge with a change request attached; (5) the matrix is release-time, not deploy-aware: no rows per environment from deployment records and no can-i-deploy gate before an apply or promotion; (6) no plan-impact analysis: an infra plan diff that changes an output the app uses, or an app change that adds an environment variable, must raise a change request in the other project; (7) no coordinated release workflow (ordering, expand and contract, shared rollback, freeze windows); (8) no environment contract test against terraform output or rendered manifests; (9) no three-way drift audit (declared in the infra repo, deployed per deployment records and cloud reads, running version and health); (10) no lifecycle workflows for decommission, rename, secret rotation (references only) and deprecation notices; (11) no on-prem and air-gapped support (Ansible inventories, Packer images, offline registry and provider mirrors, hardware leases); (12) pipeline libraries (GitHub reusable workflows, GitLab includes, Jenkins shared libraries, Azure templates) are not versioned or pinned like code libraries."""
run(["research","add","--new","--id","R-app-infra-sync","--question","How can an application project and its sister pipelines-and-infrastructure project coordinate, cooperate and be kept in sync by ddflow, and what does the planned constellation miss for that?","--claim","The planned constellation covers the version pair, change request and drift ideas, but eleven specifics for infrastructure siblings (roles, environment contract adapters, artifact handoff, sibling proposals, deploy-aware matrix, plan impact, coordinated release, contract test, three-way drift, lifecycle, on-prem) are not planned.","--mechanism",N2,"--falsifier","A read of CN-roles, CN-manifest, CN-matrix and CN-libs shows they already model environments, deployments or infrastructure contracts.","--probe","read CN-manifest, CN-matrix, CN-libs, CN-workflows, CN-dispatch, CN-adapter-* task bodies; ddflow promote --help; queue grep for environment, deployment, gitops, helm, contract","--probe-output","adapter groups: openapi, protobuf, asn1, yang/wsdl, embedded (dbc, arxml, ip-xact); no terraform, helm, kubernetes or env-schema adapter; matrix is spec@digest per release; no environment or deployment record; promote tracks branches only","--verdict","CONFIRMED","--sources","https://semaphore.io/blog/how-to-integrate-ci-cd-with-gitops-tools-like-argo-cd-or-flux; https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-02-26-argocd-environment-promotion/view; https://mattias.engineer/blog/2023/gitops-environment-promotion/; https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/discussions/5667"])

(PH1,"IA-plan-apply","Plan record and apply gate: the approved plan digest is the only thing that may be applied","SE-ask-core,TF-record,IA-stack",["ddflow/services/iac/plan*.py","tests/test_iac_plan_apply.py"],"68","A plan is evidence: plan JSON hashed and bound to the commit, variables, workspace and tool versions, expiring after a knob; an apply gate refuses anything but the digest a person (or, per the agreed agent rights, a rule) approved through the approvals engine; production apply by an agent is refused by default; state locking and a failed apply are recorded, not retried silently; no state file or secret is ever stored in the log (references and digests only)."),

(PH1,"IA-policy","Policy-as-code records: OPA/Conftest, Sentinel, Kyverno and scanner custom rules as versioned bundles with an enforce ramp and expiring waivers","SE-waiver,B-pipe-model,B-org-layers,IA-stack",["ddflow/services/iac/policy*.py","tests/test_iac_policy.py"],"69","A corporate policy is a record (owner, version, bundle source and digest, scope, severity) that maps onto the guidance pipeline effects; the shipped ramp is warn-only for N clean runs then blocking; a waiver is one scoped, reasoned, expiring record through the approvals engine; the org layer (P-org-config) distributes policies; results are findings (IA-sarif), never a bare exit code."),

(PH1,"IA-supply-chain","Supply-chain gate: signatures, provenance and SBOM verified for images and modules, digests pinned","AG-deps-guard,TD-pins,IA-decide",["ddflow/services/iac/supplychain*.py","tests/test_iac_supplychain.py"],"70","Images and modules referenced by the IaC must be pinned by digest or lock hash; cosign signatures and SLSA provenance are verified where the producer publishes them (level per the decision); an SBOM is attached to the artifact record; an unverifiable artifact is unavailable or flagged by policy, never passed; extends the dependency guard of AG-deps-guard to infrastructure artifacts."),

fields.body: Decision D-company-workflows (operator 2026-10-15, verbatim: 'Keep as a rule, that the user or company policies should be able to change anything with config, cli, mcp command, or prompt, to allow companies or projects to have specific and individual workflows'). Extends r-everything-configurable and D-universal-principles. When you add or change a feature: (1) nothing ddflow ships is a fixed policy: every workflow, pipeline, gate, role, rule, template, prompt, default, threshold and shipped record is a default that a USER or a COMPANY policy can change, per company and per project, by config file, CLI, MCP command or a plain prompt, with no code change; (2) layers are system, company (organisation config, P-org-config), project, user; a company may mark keys non-overridable below it (floors) and a project may tighten but not loosen a floor; (3) a feature that cannot be adapted this way is not done: the standards gate and reviewers check that the new behaviour has a knob or an overridable record, a way to turn it off or replace it, and tests that run with the override; (4) every change is logged and restorable from the log (config.changed, record events); (5) company defaults arrive through the org bundle and are reviewable, diffable and revertible; (6) shipped examples (workflow packs, policies, pipelines) are copied, never edited in place, so an upgrade does not overwrite a customisation.

data.summary: pytest keeps only the last 3 numbered base-temp directories per user (/tmp/pytest-of-<user>/pytest-N) and each new session removes older ones. ddflow's agents run full suites and the pre-push hook at the same time, so a LIVE session's directory is deleted by a newer session's startup. Observed 2026-10-15 in the operator's pre-push run (a clean 11763 passed, 1 error): test_contested_claim_surface setup failed 'git clone ... fatal: failed to copy file to .../pytest-15588/popen-gw35/.../b/.git/objects/maintenance.lock: No such file or directory'; the same test passes alone (11 passed). 14 pytest processes were running at that moment (five fleet agents). Fix direction: give every session its own base temp (tests/conftest.py pytest_configure sets --basetemp to a per-process unique directory unless one is given, removed at session finish) and set tmp_path_retention_count/policy so nothing else prunes it; the pre-push hook and ddflow gate runs inherit it. Regression test: start two pytest sessions at once with a retention of 1 and assert the first keeps its directory.

data.body: CORRECTED 2026-10-15. The first diagnosis (concurrent pytest sessions prune each other's tmp dirs) is NOT supported: a live session's directory is protected by pytest's lock file, and an experiment with one long session and six newer ones kept it. The single occurrence was a setup error in a test that pushes into a bare remote and clones it: 'fatal: failed to copy file to .../b/.git/objects/maintenance.lock: No such file or directory' (11763 passed, 1 error; the test passes alone). Git's local clone copies the remote's objects/ directory file by file, and auto-maintenance (git maintenance run --auto, gc --auto) started by the push takes objects/maintenance.lock while it runs: a lock that disappears between the listing and the copy fails the clone. UNPROVEN: 150 push-and-clone iterations under 8 busy loops did not reproduce it. Fix (mitigation): the suite switches git auto-maintenance off for every git process (tests/_gitquiet.py, applied in tests/conftest.py via GIT_CONFIG_COUNT). Regression test: tests/test_git_quiet_env.py (fails on the unfixed conftest). If the setup error ever recurs with maintenance off, the cause is something else: capture ls of the tmp dir at failure.

The new tests fail on the unfixed conftest (gc.auto unset).

data.body:
Fixes bug B9eeecd134c: The scheduler lists 'X is abandoned' as the reason a task is blocked but never marks the dependent as permanently stuck, and doctor is silent. 67 tasks were blocked this way on 2026-10-15 (decide tasks settled by abandon as a decision), 9 by nothing else. Fix: doctor reports a needs edge to an abandoned (not done) item with the command that drops it, and ddflow abandon of an item others need warns and lists the dependents (offering to drop the edges or re-point them). Regression test: a task needing an abandoned task is reported by doctor and abandon warns.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B9eeecd134c --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B9eeecd134c --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B9eeecd134c: A needs edge to an abandoned item blocks the dependent forever and nothing reports it as stuck

data.how: Before abandoning a decide task, list its dependents (ddflow show of the dependents, or the next output) and drop the edge; doctor will report such an edge once B9eeecd134c is fixed.
data.rule: Do not put a decide task in another task's needs; the decision record governs by globs. If one is there, drop the edge with ddflow update --needs once the decision is recorded.
data.title: A task that needs a decide task is stuck for good once the decide task is abandoned as a decision
data.why: ddflow treats an abandoned prerequisite as unsatisfied and the convention settles a decide task by abandoning it. 67 tasks waited forever on 2026-10-15 (9 on nothing else); the brief said 'X is abandoned' but nothing called it stuck.
